metaData.originalTitle: 谁是 Agent 最强守门员？首个 Agent 技能安全评测基准 SkillTrustBench 正式发布
metaData.title: Who Is the Strongest Goalkeeper for Agents? The First Agent Skill Security Evaluation Benchmark, SkillTrustBench, Officially Released
metaData.oneSentenceSummary: Tencent朱雀Lab, in collaboration with CUHK-Shenzhen, has released SkillTrustBench, the first benchmark for evaluating Agent skill security. Built from over 60,000 real skills into 5,520 test cases covering nine threat types, initial evaluations reveal the industry dilemma that high recall does not equal deployability.
metaData.summary: This article, jointly released by Tencent朱雀Lab and The Chinese University of Hong Kong, Shenzhen, officially introduces SkillTrustBench—the first dual-purpose benchmark for evaluating both the security and trustworthiness of Agent skills in real-world deployment scenarios and the detection effectiveness of external scanning solutions. The article first outlines the severe state of Agent skill security threats: the ClawHavoc incident in early 2026 led to 1,184 malicious skills being listed; a Snyk report showed 36.82% of skills had security issues; Tencent朱雀Lab's full scan revealed that 74.6% of 50,000 skills declared network request permissions, with highly decentralized external communication channels. It then points out the shortcomings of current scanning solutions: the maximum overlap of positive samples between different tools is only 10.4%, 81.9% of flagged samples are detected by only a single solution, and attackers have begun using input truncation, file type blind spots, social engineering, and other methods to bypass detection. SkillTrustBench distills 5,520 evaluation cases from 62,652 real skills, covering nine threat categories (T01-T09), with a special introduction of 'T09 Unsafe Coding Behavior' to assess skills that are non-malicious but have security flaws. The initial evaluation compared three open-source solutions—Skill Vetter, Cisco Skill Scanner, and NVIDIA SkillSpector—along with model backbones like Claude Opus 4.6, GLM 5.1, and DeepSeek V4 Flash. It found that high recall often comes with high false positives, and a truly deployable solution needs to balance recall and false positives.

mainPoints.point: Agent skill security threats have shown signs of large-scale, matrix-based production.
mainPoints.explanation: Behind 50,000 skills, the top 20 publishers collectively account for 12.9% of releases, with extreme accounts publishing an average of 10.6 skills per day. Multiple account matrices indicate the ecosystem already has the conditions for batch creation, deployment, and disguise.

mainPoints.point: Existing scanning solutions lack consensus, with extremely low overlap of positive samples.
mainPoints.explanation: OpenClaw official data shows that the maximum overlap of positive samples between any two scanning types is only 10.4%, and 81.9% of flagged samples are detected by only a single solution. The industry urgently needs a unified evaluation benchmark.

mainPoints.point: High recall does not equal deployability; false positive control is a prerequisite for production environments.
mainPoints.explanation: Cisco Skill Scanner has decent recall but a false positive rate of 24%, which can lead users to ignore security alerts. Skill Vetter + Hermes Agent has the fewest false positives and performs better overall.

mainPoints.point: Non-malicious skills also have serious security flaws.
mainPoints.explanation: A large number of normally developed skills exhibit unsafe coding behaviors such as hardcoded credentials, excessive declaration of sensitive permissions, and lack of input validation, which could be exploited by hackers through prompt injection.

keyQuotes: Being able to catch malicious samples is the first step. Being able to let normal samples pass is the prerequisite for entering the production pipeline.
Different scanning solutions see different risk facets, and there is even a lack of stable consensus on the judgment of the same batch of samples.
The core issue of Agent skill security scanning has shifted from whether there are tools to how to prove effectiveness in a new phase.

relatedArticles.title: OpenClaw and Hermes: A Comprehensive Review of AI Agent Architecture from Source Code
relatedArticles.oneSentenceSummary: This article systematically summarizes the design trade-offs and engineering practices of Agent architecture in core modules such as message routing, memory management, context engineering, and security sandboxing, through an in-depth analysis of the source code of two open-source AI Agent frameworks: OpenClaw and Hermes.

relatedArticles.title: Understanding Harness Engineering: Finding the Shell That Keeps AI from Going Rogue—Insights from 14 Engineering Articles | Hao's Trend Talk
relatedArticles.oneSentenceSummary: This article provides an in-depth analysis of "Harness Engineering," a core technology in the AI Agent field. It reveals how to compensate for model shortcomings through a three-layer management architecture and proposes the logic of "Compensation Surface Migration" that evolves with model capabilities.

relatedArticles.title: Redefining Skill Development: A Step-by-Step Guide & One-Stop Development Assistant Launch
relatedArticles.oneSentenceSummary: This article systematically introduces the concept of AI Agent Skill, including its directory structure, writing standards, release process, and cross-platform challenges. It also launches a one-stop Skill development assistant, skill-dev-aio, designed to free developers from tedious tool learning and allow them to focus on experience and judgment.

relatedArticles.title: When the Entire Team Goes Zero-Manual Coding: A 10,000-Word AI-Native Development Handbook
relatedArticles.oneSentenceSummary: This article details the Tencent team's practical experience in transitioning from AI-assisted programming to an AI-native development model, achieving a 'zero-manual coding' development loop through the OpenSpec specification and CodeBuddy toolchain.

relatedArticles.title: From Requirements to Deployment: A Comprehensive Leap in R&D Efficiency with Full AI Automation
relatedArticles.oneSentenceSummary: This article systematically explains how Tencent's audit team built a fully automated AI delivery platform to achieve end-to-end automation from requirements, design, development, testing to deployment, and shares its evolution path from L2 (human-machine collaboration) to L3 (full automation), along with core challenges, specific practices, and quantified benefits.

relatedArticles.title: Understanding Hermes in One Article: How the New Top-Tier Agent Self-Evolves from Experience
relatedArticles.oneSentenceSummary: This article provides an in-depth analysis of the core innovation of the Hermes Agent—the Skills closed-loop system—detailing its complete implementation mechanism, from experience extraction and knowledge storage to intelligent retrieval and self-improvement, along with its engineering trade-offs and security considerations.

relatedArticles.title: AI R&D Automation: Wiki Knowledge Base + Skill Pack
relatedArticles.oneSentenceSummary: This article details how to build a continuously growing team knowledge base and a supporting expert skill pack based on the LLM-Wiki model and the Obsidian platform to achieve AI-driven R&D automation.

relatedArticles.title: Harness Is Not the Goal, Knowledge Is the Moat — Knowledge Accumulation Practices of an AI Engineering Delivery Team
relatedArticles.oneSentenceSummary: Based on the engineering delivery practices of an AI Team, this article proposes that knowledge accumulation is more important than workflow orchestration, and systematically introduces a complete methodology encompassing a five-layer knowledge storage architecture, a three-level maturity system, and how workflows serve knowledge accumulation.

relatedArticles.title: Beyond Cognitive Reconstruction: Stepping into the Engineering Revolution of Agentic Engineering
relatedArticles.oneSentenceSummary: This article provides a deep dive into the practical journey of Tencent engineers transitioning from Vibe Coding to Agentic Engineering, proposing an AI-assisted engineering system centered on context management and tool-oriented design.

relatedArticles.title: Investing 10,000 RMB in AI: A Year of Tools, Practices, and Reflections
relatedArticles.oneSentenceSummary: A systematic summary of a veteran developer's practical experience in the AI wave, covering everything from MAC toolchain optimization and Harness Engineering architectural constraints to building an Agent-driven automated learning loop.
